issues.description: Older equal-rank records can overwrite newer RUNNING or terminal job data because freshness is not compared.
Rows are treated as unchanged when only state, end, and elapsed_sec match, so corrected CPU/GPU/user/partition/exit_code values are silently ignored.
Unknown or typoed states are accepted without validation, then later treated as terminal lifecycle states.
Unrecognized states default to terminal rank, which can block legitimate later active-state updates.
Negative GPU counts in AllocTRES are accepted and can produce negative GPU-hours.
Negative AllocCPUS values are accepted and can produce negative CPU-hours.
Timestamp filtering and newest-time selection use lexicographic text comparisons, which are wrong for offset-aware datetimes.
Blank User, Partition, and ExitCode fields are accepted, causing reports to group jobs under empty labels.
Report commands create a new empty database on a missing or mistyped --db path instead of warning the operator.
Report queries have no supporting indexes for reference time, state, user, or partition, so scans will become expensive as history grows.
Ingest tests do not cover same-rank out-of-order updates or corrected resource fields, leaving the main data-corruption paths untested.
